description: Apply the same modern mountain/forest glassmorphism aesthetic from the landing experience across the REST of the site: the shared UI primitives (components/ui/*), the layout shell (AppShell/Sidebar/Header), the login page, and all 16 dashboard pages. Introduce frosted translucent glass panels (backdrop-blur, subtle borders, soft highlights), harmonize the --pp-* mountain/forest tokens with the existing alpine theme, and add tasteful interactive-3D / parallax / hover effects (e.g. subtle tilt/lift on cards and stat tiles) so the whole product matches the landing's look and feel. The user grants latitude to adjust nav labels/structure/options to fit the new design, PROVIDED every existing dashboard capability stays reachable and every page stays LIVE on backend data (no regression of the real-data wiring, load/empty/error states, or the login/auth flow). Keep effects performant and usable; keep all four gates green.
steps: Restyle the shared UI primitives using the FEAT-001 glass utilities/tokens. In components/ui/Card.tsx: give the card a frosted glass surface (translucent bg + backdrop-blur + subtle --pp-mist/leaf border + soft highlight) and a tasteful hover lift/tilt (e.g. -translate-y + shadow-glass), keeping the existing title/subtitle/footer structure and class hooks tests may rely on. Update StatTile.tsx similarly (glass surface + hover lift + a mountain/forest accent bar) WITHOUT removing the label/value/hint markup the StatTile.test.tsx asserts. Update Button.tsx and Badge.tsx to the new palette but KEEP the Badge default forest tone producing class 'text-forest-800' (StatTile.test.tsx asserts this). Update Table.tsx and PageHeader.tsx for visual consistency.

Restyle the layout shell for cohesive glassmorphism. Sidebar.tsx: frosted dark glass panel over a mountain/forest gradient using --pp tokens, keep the grouped navItems rendering and active-state logic intact. Header.tsx: keep the sticky translucent backdrop-blur bar but tune to the new palette; preserve the user/session display, Badge, and Log out button behaviour. AppShell.tsx: optionally add a subtle layered mountain/forest background (CSS gradients / inline SVG silhouette, no heavy assets) behind the frosted content so pages read as glass over scenery. Keep performance reasonable (avoid full-page backdrop-blur on huge areas).

Restyle app/login/page.tsx to match the landing aesthetic: upgrade the existing alpine-gradient + mountain SVG background toward the landing's mountain/forest palette (--pp tokens), make the centered card a stronger frosted glass panel, and optionally add a subtle entrance/parallax touch — WITHOUT changing LoginForm.tsx behaviour or the demo-credential autofill/labels the LoginForm.test.tsx asserts. The login must still function and redirect into the dashboard.

Sweep the 16 dashboard pages in app/(dashboard)/ (market-radar, market-radar/unmapped-categories, time-machine, what-if, playbook, gap-finder, destination, checkout-shield, complaints, guest-compass, concierge, benchmark, forecast, proof-of-impact, authenticity, review-replies, briefing, and the relocated dashboard overview) so they adopt the restyled primitives/shell and read as glassmorphic. These pages mostly compose Card/StatTile/Table/PageHeader, so most of the restyle flows from the primitives; make per-page tweaks only where a page uses bespoke markup. CRITICAL: do NOT touch the data-fetching (useLiveData/api calls), the LoadState load/empty/error branches, or liveBadgeProps — every page must stay live on backend data with its honest load states intact.

Optionally refine the nav model in lib/theme.ts (labels/grouping/order) to better fit the new design IF it improves cohesion — but every current route must remain present and reachable (do not drop any of the 16 subsystem links, do not break the Overview/dashboard home link). If you adjust navItems, re-run the sidebar/active-route logic to confirm correctness. Keep the three theme-source files consistent.

Update any component tests whose assertions legitimately break due to intentional markup/class changes (e.g. if a wrapper class name changed), updating the assertion to the new truth WITHOUT deleting coverage. Do NOT weaken tests to pass — if a test breaks, understand why and fix the assertion or the component. The Badge default-tone and StatTile text assertions should be preserved by keeping those hooks.

Run the full gate suite and iterate until green: npm run lint, npx vitest run (all passing), npm run build (all routes compile). Then run backend uv run ruff check . + uv run pytest to confirm no cross-regression. Confirm visually-un-verifiable effects (backdrop-blur, 3D tilt) at least compile and lint cleanly, and note in findings that the glass/3D visuals need in-browser confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: UI primitives (Card, StatTile, Button, Badge, Table, PageHeader) use the mountain/forest glassmorphism tokens (frosted translucent surfaces, backdrop-blur, subtle borders) with tasteful hover lift/3D effects, while preserving the markup hooks the existing tests assert (Badge default 'text-forest-800'; StatTile label/value/hint text).
The layout shell (Sidebar, Header, AppShell) reads as cohesive glassmorphism over a mountain/forest backdrop, with session display, logout, and grouped navigation all still functioning.
The login page matches the new aesthetic with a stronger frosted-glass card while LoginForm behaviour, labels, demo-credential autofill, and dashboard redirect are unchanged.
All 16 dashboard pages render in the new glassmorphic style AND remain live on backend data with their load/empty/error states and liveBadgeProps intact (no regression of the real-data wiring).
Any nav-model adjustments keep every one of the 16 subsystem routes plus the dashboard home reachable.

npm run lint clean, npx vitest run all passing (assertions updated to new truth where markup intentionally changed, no coverage deleted), npm run build succeeds for all routes, and backend ruff + pytest (255) remain green.
verification: cd frontend && export PATH="/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH" && npm run lint && npx vitest run && npm run build
cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q

Manual static review: confirm each of the 16 dashboard page modules still calls useLiveData/api and renders LoadState branches (grep for useLiveData / LoadState usage unchanged), and that primitives reference the new glass utilities.
findings:
Applied the mountain/forest glassmorphism + interactive-3D aesthetic across the rest of the site, reusing the FEAT-001 tokens/utilities (.glass-panel, .glass-panel--dark, pp-* colors). All changes flow from the shared primitives and the layout shell, so NO dashboard page module was touched: `git diff` shows only app/globals.css, app/login/page.tsx, components/layout/{AppShell,Header,Sidebar}.tsx and components/ui/{Card,StatTile,Button,Badge,Table}.tsx. Live-data wiring is fully intact: all 17 page.tsx (16 subsystems + Overview) still use useLiveData, LoadState, and liveBadgeProps (verified by grep post-change), and LoadState itself renders through the restyled Card so its load/empty/error panels pick up the glass look automatically.

globals.css additions (additive, @layer components): (1) a `.glass-lift` / `.glass-lift-inner` interactive-3D primitive — perspective wrapper + inner element that lifts (-4px) and tilts (rotateX 2.5deg / rotateY -2.5deg, scale 1.012) with a sharper glass shadow on hover; (2) a `.pp-scenery` app-shell backdrop (soft daylight misty-ridge gradient over --pp-mist with leaf/amber alpenglow radial glows — intentionally LIGHT so the existing dark forest-800 text and the frosted light-glass cards both stay readable; a dark scenery would have tanked legibility of the un-paneled PageHeader text). Added a prefers-reduced-motion block that disables the tilt/lift transform for users who opt out.

Primitives: Card now uses `.glass-panel .glass-lift` with a `.glass-lift-inner` wrapper (frosted translucent bg-mist-white/70, backdrop-blur, pp-mist border, soft highlight) and a tasteful hover lift/tilt, keeping the title/subtitle/footer structure and children intact. StatTile gets the same glass+lift surface with a mountain/forest accent bar (leaf -> moss -> amber inline gradient) and KEEPS the label/value/hint markup StatTile.test asserts. Button primary = deep pp-forest fill with glass shadow + hover lift, secondary = frosted translucent backdrop-blur surface, ghost tuned to pp-mist. Badge recolored to translucent frosted pills but the DEFAULT forest tone still produces class 'text-forest-800' (StatTile.test assertion preserved). Table = `.glass-panel` surface, frosted header, pp-leaf/10 row hover. PageHeader left structurally intact (reads cleanly over the light scenery).

Shell: AppShell wraps content in `.pp-scenery` with a lightweight inline-SVG distant ridge silhouette (no raster asset), content layered above at z-10. Sidebar converted from the solid bg-forest-header to a `.glass-panel--dark` frosted dark panel over a pp forest-to-stone gradient, with grouped navItems rendering and active-route logic unchanged (active pill now uses pp-leaf accent). Header keeps the sticky translucent backdrop-blur bar, retuned to pp-mist/mist-white with stronger blur+saturate; user/session display, property Badge, and Log out button behaviour unchanged. Login page: background moved to the pp palette (slate->forest->moss->amber), glow blobs -> pp-leaf/pp-amber, mountain SVG silhouette recolored to pp hues, and the centered card upgraded to a stronger frosted glass panel (bg-mist-white/60 + backdrop-blur-2xl + saturate + shadow-glass). LoginForm.tsx was NOT changed, so labels, demo-credential autofill, and the push('/dashboard') redirect all still work (LoginForm.test green).

Nav model: left navItems/groups/order unchanged — every one of the 16 subsystem routes plus the /dashboard Overview home remains present and reachable; no nav/option changes were needed for cohesion.

Gates (all green): frontend `npm run lint` clean, `npx vitest run` 24 passing (6 files — StatTile Badge 'text-forest-800', StatTile label/value/hint, deep-pages/sentinel titles, and LoginForm redirect all still pass, no assertions changed or coverage removed), `npm run build` succeeds with 23 generated routes (same count as after FEAT-002: / + /_not-found + /login + 20 dashboard pages). Backend `uv run ruff check .` clean and `uv run pytest -q` 255 passing — unaffected.

BROWSER-ONLY ITEMS (cannot be visually verified in this sandbox — no display, dev servers blocked): the backdrop-filter frosted-glass blur on all panels, the interactive-3D hover tilt/lift (.glass-lift), the pp-scenery radial glows, and the login frosted card all COMPILE and LINT cleanly and are statically correct, but their rendered appearance and the prefers-reduced-motion behaviour need in-browser confirmation. Committed on branch main (no push).
